column1: # Decisions of the case party under Paper 4, Section 8.2 (spec/SENTENCES.md); format: FORMATS.md "Decisions".
# PATTERN<TAB>CLASS<TAB>SENTENCE_ID<TAB>REASON. The first matching rule wins. An object with "exec": true is never
# excluded by any rule (S8.2-9, S8.2-10). A "runtime" rule never excludes by itself: compare resolves the program or
# setting that creates the object and excludes it only if that creator is recorded; otherwise the object is reported
# with the creator named. Every excluded object is written to compare-excluded.tsv.
# S8.2-5: "What exists only while the computer runs—a process, an open port, a mount point, a relationship between
# services—is not considered a separate object: it belongs to the program or setting that creates it, and the
# decision follows that for the program or setting."

column4: whether a unit is running, and which processes run in it, exists only while the computer runs; the unit itself is still compared on enabled, load, fragment, source, drop-ins and transient
a process belongs to its executable (the id is the path read from /proc/PID/exe); decided with that file; kernel threads with the kernel image of the running release
an open port belongs to the executable of the process that holds it
a mount point belongs to what creates it: the file behind its loop device, else the fstab file or the unit file the service manager names for it; if none is named the mount is reported
a loaded kernel module belongs to its module file (modinfo -n)
a login-session scope is a relationship between the processes of one login, created when they start and gone when they end; decided with the executables of its member processes

column1: # Added 2026-11-24, 13:55–15:50 UTC ([n3-A]). Used only by `compare --questions`, which the runner gives to
# every comparison of an installation. An object of the writable area (a filesystem or image mounted read-write, or a
# volatile filesystem) that follows from no line is decided by the four questions of S8.2-6 in their order:
# question 1 by the `store` rules below; question 2 by the routes (routes.tsv: a direct route of the object's form
# executes it); then the rules above that name the program which recorded the object; question 3 by the `carrier/...`
# rules below, each with the probe that shows whether the setting is in force; otherwise S8.2-15: a program record
# or material, not counted (compare-excluded.tsv, rule `four-questions`). The stored, read-only system part is not
# decided this way: there every object that equals neither the derivation nor the reference installation stays
# Question 1, S8.2-7: "Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a
# package and does it remain as received?" Where package managers keep what they install.

column1: # Question 3, S8.2-11 to S8.2-14: "Is the object a value chosen by a person that the computer as a whole obeys ...?";
# "A value obeyed only by a program that a person runs for himself or herself is a setting if it launches something
# or grants access". Where settings are stored, by the probe that shows one in force (compare, function `probe`):
# carrier/unit: the service manager loaded a unit from it (the units of the inventory: file, source, drop-ins; a
# symlink in a .wants/.requires folder: the unit it names is enabled); carrier/cron: a running cron daemon reads it
# (the cron tables of the inventory); carrier/key: the SSH server takes a key from it (the authorized keys of the
# inventory); carrier/route: the program that obeys it executed it (routes.tsv: a direct route of its form);
# carrier/none: no probe exists in the case party's programs, the outcome is UNPROBED ([n3-B]).
